reasoning: All three numerator base functions E, rho, and expNegInvGlue are defined by exactly the same two branches on the real line, using exp(-1/s) for s>0 and 0 otherwise.

Every denominator is strictly positive: for any real s, at least one of s or 1-s is positive, and the corresponding exp(-1/u) is positive. Pinned mathlib theorem Real.smoothTransition.pos_denom records this.

Substitution of identical numerator and denominator expressions yields pointwise equality of beta, sigma, and Real.smoothTransition for all s; substituting s=2*t-1 yields the stationary ramp equality for all t.

The October slow scalar alpha_1(t)=sigma(2t-1)/(1+t) is NOT equal to startupRamp(t) in general; for t>=1 it is (1+t)^-1 whereas startupRamp(t)=1. The identity here concerns the common startup transition sigma(2t-1), not the slow profile alpha_1.
